judgment.notes: Checked every displayed M application, conditionally on its supplied contract. M008 uses the finite tensor images of the generators; S002 proves their span is U. M002 uses R⊂ℚ as algebra and the N002 basis m reindexed by the finite I of cardinality n; its conclusion supplies the base-changed basis, not merely a dimension assertion. M010 applies to nontrivial commutative ℚ in both S003 and S004. M003 then computes finrank T from that basis. For M004 the family is constantly U on I: S002 supplies finite generation explicitly, M009 supplies freeness over ℚ, and M010 supplies strong rank condition. M005 uses Θ with the explicitly verified inverse Ψ. M001 uses the singleton 1⊗a, whose independence is proved by μ and a≠0, with dimension one from F004 and finite dimensionality from F002. Both M007 applications use nonzero naturals |A| and B and p≠1 from primality. The resulting factors are proved nonzero and the unit and its inverse satisfy the defining R denominator condition. BG001–BG007 verify the routine tensor applications with their scalar towers and module conditions. No E applications occur.

S001 correctly uses matrix-unit stability to identify every J_i with J and to show that finitely many coordinates of m generate J. If J=0, all coordinates of M_R vanish, contrary to its complex span containing the nonzero e_0; 0∈I follows from H001. Its coordinate maps are inverse R-linear maps. In S002 the common-denominator calculation uses H_l∈ℤ⊂R, not an unwarranted assumption 1/D∈R; the product of positive denominators is nonzero, including the empty presentation. Thus μ(z)=0 forces the single remaining J coefficient to vanish, proving injectivity; the image is precisely the rational span. S003 computes dim T=n. S004 constructs both tensor maps and checks both composites on pure tensors and finite coordinate sums; verified tensor generation extends these identities everywhere. M004 and M005 give n=n·dim U, and n>0 gives dim U=1. S005 uses μ to prove singleton independence and obtains the nonzero rational multiples of a. S006 obtains integer exponents and R-units by the supplied M007, with all denominators nonzero. S007 takes a minimum of a nonempty finite integer list, constructs nonzero b=p^νa, proves both inclusions J=Rb, and proves spanning and independence of (b e_i). The same argument establishes the universal clause for every nonzero generator b. The case λ=0 gives n=1 and requires no exception.
